282: Even thinking in your mind, “I will steal what belongs to someone else,” is wrong.
283: Wealth gained by stealing may seem to grow without limit, but it will soon disappear.
284: A strong wish to gain by stealing will, in the end, bring sorrow that never ends.
285: People who only want other people's things, and wait for them to look away, cannot have real kindness or love.
286: People who are deeply in love with stealing cannot live within what is right and fair.
287: Stealing is a dark, sneaky skill. People who have chosen the strength of living within what is fair do not have it.
288: Goodness stays firmly in the hearts of people who know what is fair. In the same way, sneaky deceit stays in the hearts of people who know only stealing.
289: People who know nothing except stealing will be ruined right in the middle of the wrong things they do.
290: Thieves lose even their own lives. People who never steal will not miss out on heaven (the world of the gods).
